_comment: marble_arch: a free-standing archway for Map 2 (marble), a blockout prop placed by hand. Two piers carrying a round arch -- 4.00 m across, 5.00 m tall, 1.20 m thick at the panel, 1.44 at the piers and 1.64 at the socle and cornice; the opening is 2.20 m wide and 3.00 m to the crown, so a runner goes through at speed. Origin is the BASE CENTRE: z=0 (Godot y=0) is the ground it stands on, x runs across the face and the passage runs along y, so Blender's `front` view is the face a runner meets. The head is marble_wall_build's arch -- a semicircle off a straight jamb, the reveal in `shade`, cut at 2 x marble_build.HEAD_SEG segments because a runner passes through this one rather than looking at it across the rotunda -- and the mouldings are the rotunda wall's, scaled to five metres: a 0.70 m socle band 0.22 proud (`plinth`), the opening cut through it so each pier stands on its own block, the wall's pilaster the full width of each 0.70 m pier, 0.12 proud and fluted (`column`), a recessed panel the arch is cut in (`marble` / `marble2`) and a 0.85 m cornice 0.22 proud on the socle's own line, `band` over a `shade` soffit. ONE CONTIGUOUS MESH: the stone is an axis-aligned cell complex on three shared station lists plus the arch's rays from the springing centre, so every face lands on a grid line both sides agree on and marble_build._Mesh.v welds it -- one component, every edge on exactly two faces, no duplicate positions. One material, marble's packed 256 px atlas. MarbleArchCollision rides in the .glb as a `-colonly` node drawn from the same arch profile (one closed solid on the same station lists -- the socle out to x +-2.22 by y +-0.82, the piers and the arch at x +-2.00 by y +-0.72, the opening cut clean through ray for ray; the panel's 0.12 m recess and the cornice's 0.22 m overhang are collapsed onto the pier line), so the passage is actually passable; Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `surfaces` and `max_tris` count only what is drawn.
